mainTopic: Removing חמץ on ערב פסח that falls on שבת or while traveling, which meals count as a סעודת מצוה, and choosing a fitting marriage
overview: This amud opens with a משנה about ערב פסח that falls on שבת. רבי מאיר says all חמץ is destroyed on Friday, חכמים say it is removed at its usual time, and רבי אליעזר בר צדוק splits between תרומה and חולין. A ברייתא then tells of חמץ being removed on שבת itself in יבנה. A second משנה teaches what a person should do if he is on the way to a מצוה, to save lives, or on an optional trip and remembers he has חמץ at home. It also covers someone who left ירושלים with בשר קודש, and it ends with a dispute about the minimum amount that makes a person go back. The גמרא asks why the משנה treats a סעודת אירוסין as a מצוה when a ברייתא calls it optional. It answers in two ways: by assigning the sources to רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, or, following רב חסדא, by splitting between the first and second meal. This leads to רבי שמעון's rule that a תלמיד חכם should not enjoy a meal that is not a מצוה. Next come teachings and stories about marrying a כהן's daughter, warnings about feasting, and advice to marry into a scholar's family. That last ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: destroy all the חמץ before שבת
steps.stepSummary: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, רבי מאיר rules that all חמץ is destroyed before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, we destroy all the חמץ before שבת. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new case: the day before פסח falls on שבת. רבי מאיר gives the first opinion, which is to get rid of everything early, on Friday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally חמץ is destroyed on the fourteenth itself. On שבת we cannot burn it, so רבי מאיר moves the destruction to Friday for everything, both תרומה and חולין. He only leaves out what is needed for the שבת meals.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: MISHNA: The fourteenth (of Nisan) that falls on Shabbat —
we remove everything before Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Except what is needed for the Shabbat meals.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, when ערב פסח is on שבת, all חמץ (תרומה and חולין) is destroyed on Friday.

steps.title: The Sages: destroy it at its usual time
steps.stepSummary: חכמים rule that the חמץ is destroyed at its usual time, on the fourteenth itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: at its usual time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second opinion. חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and say we do not move the removal earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים hold that the חמץ is removed on שבת morning at the normal time. This is done without burning, for example by giving it away or declaring it ownerless.

keyTerms.meaning: At its usual time, on the fourteenth

steps.confusionAlert: חכמים do not mean the חמץ is burned on שבת. Burning is forbidden on שבת. 'At its time' means getting rid of it in a way that is allowed on שבת.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: at its (usual) time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי מאיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ is removed on the fourteenth itself, even when it falls on שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק splits תרומה from regular food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says תרומה is destroyed before שבת, but חולין at its usual time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says: תרומה before שבת, and חולין at its usual time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third, middle opinion. It treats תרומה differently from ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only כהנים may eat תרומה, so it may not get finished on שבת, and it cannot be given to just anyone. That is why it should be destroyed on Friday. Ordinary food (חולין) can easily be eaten or given away on שבת, so it waits for the usual time.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion given to a כהן, which only כהנים may eat
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions. רבי מאיר says everything before שבת. חכמים say everything at its time. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says תרומה before שבת and חולין at its time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says:
Teruma — before Shabbat,
and non-sacred food — at their (usual) time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A compromise between the first two opinions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה is destroyed on Friday, and חולין on the fourteenth itself.

steps.title: A story in יבנה: חמץ removed on שבת itself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי אליעזר בר צדוק and his father destroyed חמץ in יבנה on שבת when the fourteenth fell on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא that רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says: Once my father spent שבת in יבנה, and the fourteenth fell on שבת. זונין, the official appointed by רבן גמליאל, came and said, 'The time has come to remove the חמץ.' I went with my father, and we removed the חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life story as evidence. In it, חמץ was removed on שבת itself, at the usual time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing חמץ on the fourteenth even though it was שבת fits the view that חמץ is removed 'at its time' (חכמים, and רבי אליעזר בר צדוק for חולין). It also shows this was the actual practice under רבן גמליאל's leadership in יבנה, not only a theory.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
יבנה, the center of Torah leadership after the Churban

steps.whyThisMatters: A מעשה (actual event) carries weight in הלכה. Here it shows that removing חמץ on שבת at the regular time was really done.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught (in a baraita),
Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says:
One time my father spent Shabbat in Yavne,
and the fourteenth fell on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא זוּנִין מְמוּנֶּה שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: And Zonin, the appointee of Rabban Gamliel, came

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: הִגִּיעַ עֵת לְבַעֵר אֶת הֶחָמֵץ,
phrases.english: and said: The time has come to remove the chametz,
and I went with my father
and we removed the chametz.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: פַּעַם אַחַת
steps.raayaObject: That חמץ is removed at its usual time even when the fourteenth falls on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording an actual event in יבנה under רבן גמליאל

steps.title: On the way to a מצוה and remembering חמץ at home
steps.stepSummary: Someone on the way to a מצוה who remembers he has חמץ at home should go back if he has time to destroy it and still do the מצוה. If not, he cancels it in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone going to slaughter his קרבן פסח, or to circumcise his son, or to eat a betrothal meal at his father-in-law's house, remembers that he has חמץ in his house. If he can go back, destroy it, and still return to his מצוה, he should go back and destroy it. If not, he cancels it in his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A person is traveling to an important מצוה and suddenly remembers he left חמץ at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מצוות count, so the משנה tries to let him do both. If time allows, he physically destroys the חמץ. If going back would make him miss the מצוה, ביטול (canceling it in his heart) is enough according to Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: He cancels it in his heart, declaring it worthless and ownerless

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who is going to slaughter his Paschal lamb,
or to circumcise his son,
or to eat a betrothal meal at his father-in-law's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חָמֵץ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: and he remembers that he has chametz in his house.
If he is able to go back and remove it
and return to his מצוה —
he should go back and remove it,
and if not — he nullifies it in his heart.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a מצוה trip, go back to destroy the חמץ only if the מצוה will not be lost. Otherwise ביטול is enough.

steps.title: On the way to save lives: just nullify it
steps.stepSummary: Someone going to rescue people from danger does not go back at all. He cancels the חמץ in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is going to rescue people from גוים, from a river, from bandits, from a fire, or from a collapsed building, he should cancel the חמץ in his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a more urgent case: rescuing people in danger. Here the answer is simply to cancel the חמץ in his heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the previous case, there is no 'if he can go back.' Saving lives is so urgent that he should not delay at all, even if he could make it home and back in time.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not carry over the 'if he can go back' rule from the previous case. When lives are at stake, he never goes back.

phrases.english: To rescue from gentiles, or from a river,
or from bandits, or from a fire,
or from a collapsed building —
he should nullify it in his heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A more urgent case, with an unconditional rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When going to save lives, he does not go back. ביטול alone is enough.

steps.title: On an optional שבת-boundary trip: go back right away
steps.stepSummary: Someone going to set up an optional שבת residence (עירוב תחומין) must go back immediately to destroy his חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is going to set up an optional שבת residence, he should go back immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the least important case, a trip that is not for a מצוה. Here he must go back right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting up a שביתת הרשות (an עירוב תחומין for personal convenience) is not a מצוה, so it gives no reason to rely on ביטול alone. The מצוה of destroying חמץ comes first, so he goes back immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting a שבת residence for an optional, non-מצוה purpose

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. For a מצוה trip, go back only if there is time. To save lives, never go back; use ביטול. For an optional trip, always go back right away.

phrases.english: And to establish an optional Shabbat residence —
he should go back immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite extreme from the life-saving case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a non-מצוה trip, he must go back immediately to destroy the חמץ.

steps.title: Someone who left Jerusalem carrying consecrated meat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a parallel case. A person who left ירושלים with בשר קודש burns it where he is if he has passed צופים. If not, he goes back and burns it in front of the בירה using wood from the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to someone who left ירושלים and remembered he had בשר קודש with him. If he already passed צופים, he burns it where he is. If not, he goes back and burns it in front of the בירה (the בית המקדש), using wood from the מערכה on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case that works like the חמץ case. It is about holy meat that has left ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בשר קודש that leaves ירושלים becomes פסול and must be burned. The משנה uses a distance marker, צופים, the spot past which you can no longer see ירושלים. Before that point, he must return and burn it at the מקדש. After that point, he does not need to go back.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy meat from a קרבן, which may be eaten only inside ירושלים
Mount Scopus, the spot past which ירושלים can no longer be seen
Wood from the pile set up on the מזבח

phrases.english: And similarly, one who left Jerusalem
and remembered that he had holy meat with him,
if he passed Mount Scopus,
phrases.notes: Past this point the city can no longer be seen.

phrases.english: he burns it where he is.
And if not, he goes back and burns it
in front of the Temple, with wood from the altar pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the חמץ rules in steps 5 to 7. It uses the same idea of going back versus not going back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before צופים, he goes back and burns the בשר קודש at the מקדש. After צופים, he burns it where he is.

steps.title: How much requires going back: a three-way dispute
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how large an amount makes a person go back. רבי מאיר says a כביצה for both cases. רבי יהודה says a כזית for both. חכמים say a כזית for בשר קודש but a כביצה for חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must there be for them to go back? רבי מאיר says: in both cases, a כביצה. רבי יהודה says: in both cases, a כזית. חכמים say: for בשר קודש, a כזית; for חמץ, a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by setting a minimum size that makes a person turn around, for both the חמץ case and the holy-meat case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question applies to both cases together. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each treat both cases the same, one with a larger measure and one with a smaller one. חכמים split them: the smaller measure, כזית, for holy meat, and the larger measure, כביצה, for חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The volume of an egg, the larger measure
The volume of an olive, the smaller measure
This one and that one, meaning both cases

steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions: רבי מאיר says כביצה for both. רבי יהודה says כזית for both. חכמים say כזית for בשר קודש and כביצה for חמץ.

phrases.english: And for how much do they go back?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: זֶה וְזֶה בִּכְבֵיצָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: in both cases, for an egg's volume,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זֶה וְזֶה בִּכְזַיִת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: in both cases, for an olive's volume.
And the Sages say: for holy meat, an olive's volume,
and for חמץ, an egg's volume.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the minimum amounts for the going-back rules given in steps 5 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת about the minimum amount: כביצה, כזית, or a split between the two cases.

steps.title: A teaching that contradicts the משנה about a betrothal meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says that someone going to a סעודת אירוסין at his father-in-law's house, or going to set up a שביתת הרשות, must go back immediately. This clashes with the משנה, which treated the betrothal meal as a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: And they raised a contradiction. One who goes to eat a סעודת אירוסין at his father-in-law's house, or to set up an optional שבת residence, must go back immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out a contradiction. A ברייתא treats the betrothal meal as merely optional, while our משנה treated it as a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, the betrothal meal was listed among מצוה trips. For those, if there is no time, he cancels the חמץ in his heart instead of going back. The ברייתא groups the same meal with the optional שביתה case from step 7 and says he must go back immediately. The two sources disagree on how to treat the same meal.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction against it, meaning a contrasting source is brought
Setting up a Shabbat residence for an optional purpose

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not about the שביתה case, which both sources treat as optional. It is only about the betrothal meal: our משנה counts it as a מצוה, while the ברייתא treats it as optional.

phrases.english: Gemara: And they raised a contradiction:
One who goes to eat a betrothal meal
at his father-in-law's house,
or to set up an optional Shabbat residence,
must go back immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by contrasting the משנה's treatment of the betrothal meal with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of the סעודת אירוסין as a מצוה trip, where one may cancel the חמץ in his heart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the betrothal meal as optional and requires going back immediately, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there is no difficulty. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and the משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה; that one follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction by assigning each source to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources really do disagree, but that is fine because they reflect a known מחלוקת תנאים. The ברייתא, which calls the meal optional, is רבי יהודה. The משנה, which calls the meal a מצוה, is רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... that one, used to assign each source to a different opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It is not difficult:
this one (the ברייתא) follows Rabbi Yehuda,
that one (the משנה) follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: the two sources reflect a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seem to state one shared ruling, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says the meal is optional. The משנה follows רבי יוסי, who says it is a מצוה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about the betrothal meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the מחלוקת directly. רבי יהודה says a סעודת אירוסין is רשות, and רבי יוסי says it is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A betrothal meal is optional; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: it is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the מחלוקת רבי יוחנן relied on really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer depends on this specific disagreement. The ברייתא states it openly: for רבי יהודה the meal is optional, so one must go back. For רבי יוסי it is a מצוה, so one may cancel the חמץ in his heart.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a סעודת אירוסין is a מצוה is a מחלוקת between רבי יהודה (רשות) and רבי יוסי (מצוה). Our משנה follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: As it was taught: A betrothal meal is optional,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: it is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer in step 11 by showing that the מחלוקת exists.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree about the status of the betrothal meal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording that the meal is רשות according to רבי יהודה and a מצוה according to רבי יוסי

steps.title: A second answer: first meal versus second meal
steps.stepSummary: Based on רב חסדא, the משנה and the ברייתא can both follow רבי יהודה. The משנה talks about the first betrothal meal, which everyone agrees is a מצוה. The ברייתא talks about the second meal, which רבי יהודה holds is only רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that רב חסדא said: 'The argument is only about the second meal, but everyone agrees the first meal is a מצוה,' you can even say that both the משנה and the ברייתא follow רבי יהודה, and there is no difficulty. This one is about the first meal, and that one is about the second meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to solve the contradiction from Step 10, without needing to say the two sources follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer split the sources between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. רב חסדא limits their argument to the second meal only, since everyone agrees the first meal is a מצוה. So the משנה, which calls the meal a מצוה, means the first meal. The ברייתא, which says to go back, means the second meal, and both fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that [someone] said: introduces a new answer built on a later statement
The second betrothal meal, an extra meal with the bride's family
This one and that one: both sources

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel רבי יוחנן's answer. It is another possible answer. In the new answer the משנה no longer follows רבי יוסי. Both sources follow רבי יהודה, and they differ only in WHICH meal each one is talking about.

phrases.english: And now that Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about the second meal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּסְעוּדָה רִאשׁוֹנָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מִצְוָה.
phrases.english: but the first meal, all agree, is a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא הָא וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Even if you say this and that both follow Rabbi Yehuda,
it is not difficult:
this (the Mishnah) is about the first meal,
that (the Baraita) is about the second meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second solution to the contradiction that רבי יוחנן solved in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): first meal versus second meal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא must follow different תנאים, רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both can follow רבי יהודה. The משנה refers to the first meal, which is a מצוה for everyone. The ברייתא refers to the second meal, which רבי יהודה treats as רשות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a contradiction can be solved either by assigning sources to different תנאים or by defining their cases differently.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about the gifts meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה counts only the betrothal meal as a מצוה, not the meal for giving gifts (סבלונות). רבי יוסי counts both as a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said, 'I only heard about the betrothal meal, but not about the gifts meal.' רבי יוסי said to him, 'I heard about both the betrothal meal and the gifts meal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same two תנאים. This time they argue about the meal held when the groom gives the bride gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats the gifts meal as a regular, optional meal. רבי יוסי extends מצוה status to it as well. This fits each one's general approach: רבי יוסי is broader in calling these meals a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Gifts the groom sends the bride, along with a meal held for the occasion

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶלָּא סְעוּדַת אֵירוּסִין,
phrases.english: I only heard (that it is a מצוה) about a betrothal meal,
but not about the gifts meal.
Rabbi Yosei said to him:
I heard about both a betrothal meal and the gifts meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֲנִי לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶלָּא סְעוּדַת אֵירוּסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another related argument between the same two תנאים about which meals count as a מצוה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, only the betrothal meal is a מצוה, not the gifts meal. According to רבי יוסי, both are a מצוה.

steps.title: A Torah scholar should not enjoy a meal that is not a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that a תלמיד חכם may not benefit from any meal that is not a סעודת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון says, 'Any meal that is not a meal of מצוה, a תלמיד חכם is not allowed to enjoy it.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is which meals count as a מצוה, the גמרא brings a related ברייתא. It teaches that a Torah scholar should stay away from meals that are not a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why the question of whether a meal is a מצוה matters in practice. It decides whether a תלמיד חכם may attend. The rule is general, so the גמרא will next ask what kind of meal is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal that is a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical reason it matters whether a meal counts as a מצוה: it determines whether a scholar may take part.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any meal that is not a מצוה meal,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רַשַּׁאי לֵהָנוֹת מִמֶּנָּה.
phrases.english: a Torah scholar is not permitted to benefit from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל סְעוּדָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which meals are a מצוה to how this affects a תלמיד חכם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may not benefit from a meal that is not a סעודת מצוה.

steps.title: What kind of meal is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an example of a meal that is not a מצוה, according to רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question to set up the next step: what is an example of the kind of meal רבי שמעון means?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in Step 15 is very general. The גמרא wants a concrete case, especially since wedding meals are usually a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, what? (a request for a concrete case)

phrases.english: For example, what?
phrases.notes: A short setup question asking for a concrete case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the rule in Step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of a meal that is not a מצוה, which a תלמיד חכם should avoid

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's examples: mismatched marriages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives two examples: a כהן's daughter marrying a ישראל, and a תלמיד חכם's daughter marrying an עם הארץ. The wedding meals for these marriages are not a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'For example, a כהן's daughter who marries a ישראל, and a תלמיד חכם's daughter who marries an עם הארץ.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by naming two kinds of weddings whose meal does not count as a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding meal is normally a מצוה. In these cases the match is considered unfitting, so the meal loses that status. A תלמיד חכם should therefore not join it.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular Jew who is not a כהן or לוי

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the marriage is forbidden. The marriage is fully valid. It only means the meal does not count as a סעודת מצוה, so a scholar should not attend.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For example, a priest's daughter (marrying) an Israelite,
and a Torah scholar's daughter (marrying) an unlearned man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wedding meal of a כהן's daughter to a ישראל, or of a תלמיד חכם's daughter to an עם הארץ, is not a סעודת מצוה.

steps.title: Why a priest's daughter marrying an Israelite is not a מצוה meal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the first example with another statement of רבי יוחנן: when a כהן's daughter marries a ישראל, the marriage does not turn out well.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: 'A כהן's daughter who marries a ישראל, their match does not go well.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first example counts as a meal that is not a מצוה, using another teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוחנן holds that such a marriage will not succeed, its meal cannot be a celebration of a מצוה. This is the reason behind the example in Step 17.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a meal is a מצוה matters in two places: whether you must go back to destroy חמץ (the משנה), and whether a תלמיד חכם may attend (רבי שמעון). According to רבי יוחנן, an unfitting match makes the wedding meal not a מצוה.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
A priest's daughter (marrying) an Israelite,
their match does not turn out well.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason for the first example in Step 17
steps.raayaObject: That the wedding of a כהן's daughter to a ישראל is not a סעודת מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that such a match does not turn out well

steps.title: What does 'not turning out well' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly goes wrong when a כהן's daughter marries a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן meant when he said this marriage does not turn out well. This short question sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 gave only a general warning. Here the גמרא asks for concrete details: what kind of bad outcome is meant?

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request to explain a statement)

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: What does 'the marriage does not turn out well' actually mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific bad outcome comes from a בת כהן marrying a ישראל?

steps.title: רב חסדא: widow, divorcee, or childless
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that she will become a widow, a divorcee, or be left without children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Either she will be a 'widow,' or a 'divorcee,' or 'she has no children.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He lists three bad outcomes, taken from the words of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words come from ויקרא 22:13. That פסוק describes a בת כהן who married a non-כהן and returns to her father's house as a widow, a divorcee, or childless. רב חסדא reads the פסוק as hinting at what such marriages tend to lead to.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the statement

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Either a 'widow,' or a 'divorcee,'
or 'she has no children.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The marriage leads to widowhood, divorce, or childlessness, as hinted in ויקרא 22:13.

steps.title: A ברייתא: early death or poverty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one spouse will bury the other, or she will make him poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: He will bury her, or she will bury him, or she will bring him to poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another version of the bad outcomes. One of them will die young, or the husband will become poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second description alongside רב חסדא's. It adds poverty to the list. That detail sets up the coming challenge, because רבי יוחנן elsewhere says that marrying into כהונה brings wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He will bury her, or she will bury him,
phrases.notes: One of them will die young

phrases.english: or she will bring him to poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation, from a ברייתא, next to רב חסדא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bad outcome is that one spouse dies early, or the husband becomes poor.

steps.title: But marrying into אהרן's family brings wealth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with רבי יוחנן's own teaching that clinging to the children of אהרן makes a person rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי יוחנן said: One who wants to become rich should cling to the descendants of אהרן, and all the more so, since Torah and כהונה make them rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. רבי יוחנן said this marriage goes badly, but he also said marrying into a כהן's family brings wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said this match does not turn out well, and the ברייתא explained that she may even bring him to poverty. Yet רבי יוחנן himself also says that marrying into אהרן's family brings wealth, so his two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Cling to the descendants of אהרן (marry into a כהן's family)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
One who wants to become rich
should cling to the descendants of Aaron,
all the more so, since Torah and priesthood make them rich.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea in steps 18 to 21 that such a marriage is unlucky.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that a בת כהן marrying a ישראל does not turn out well, including the danger of poverty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself says that marrying into the family of אהרן brings wealth, which is the opposite outcome.

steps.title: Torah scholar versus ignoramus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a תלמיד חכם who marries a כהנת becomes rich, but an עם הארץ does not do well.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: this one is about a תלמיד חכם, and that one is about an עם הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. Each teaching of רבי יוחנן applies to a different kind of husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing of wealth applies when a תלמיד חכם marries a כהן's daughter. The warning applies when an עם הארץ marries her. This matches the 'Torah and כהונה' phrase: the blessing comes when both are joined together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Marrying a כהן's daughter brings blessing to a תלמיד חכם but not to an עם הארץ.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about a Torah scholar,
that one is about an ignoramus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by type of husband)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings of רבי יוחנן seemed to contradict each other about every marriage to a כהנת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wealth is for a תלמיד חכם who marries a כהנת; misfortune is for an עם הארץ.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's humble reaction to illness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע married a כהנת and became sick. He said אהרן must not want a son-in-law like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע married a כהן's daughter and became ill. He said: אהרן is not pleased that I cling to his descendants, that he should have a son-in-law like me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי יהושע. He married a כהנת, fell ill, and blamed himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע was a great תלמיד חכם, so by the rule in step 23 his marriage should have been blessed. Out of humility, he concluded that he was not worthy enough to count as a fitting son-in-law for אהרן.
steps.confusionAlert: This story does not disprove step 23. רבי יהושע is speaking in humility, judging himself as not a true תלמיד חכם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua married a priest's daughter and became ill.
He said: Aaron is not pleased
that I cling to his descendants,
that he should have a son-in-law like me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of step 23 through a story of a sage who felt unworthy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע understood his illness after marrying a כהנת as a sign that he was not worthy, which assumes that worthy scholars are blessed.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין's two ordained sons
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין married a כהנת and had two ordained sons, רב ששת and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין married a כהן's daughter, and two ordained sons came from him: רב ששת son of רב אידי, and רבי יהושע son of רב אידי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the blessing of a scholar who married a כהנת. He was blessed with sons who became ordained rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports step 23: when a תלמיד חכם marries into כהונה, the marriage is blessed. Here the blessing came in the form of Torah greatness in his children.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who married a כהנת
Ordained (given סמיכה to rule on halacha)

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין נָסֵיב כָּהֵנְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin married a priest's daughter,
and two ordained sons came from him:
Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi,
and Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rav Idi.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין נָסֵיב כָּהֵנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a positive example that matches the תלמיד חכם case of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That a תלמיד חכם who marries a כהנת is blessed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אידי בר אבין's two ordained sons

steps.title: רב פפא became rich through marrying a כהנת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא said that he became wealthy only because he married a כהן's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If I had not married a כהן's daughter, I would not have become rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב פפא's personal testimony. He credits his wealth to marrying a כהנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This directly confirms רבי יוחנן's teaching from step 22 that clinging to אהרן's descendants brings wealth. Because רב פפא was a תלמיד חכם, it also fits the answer in step 23.
steps.whatToRemember: The stories confirm the conclusion: a תלמיד חכם who marries a כהנת is blessed with Torah children and wealth.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If I had not married a priest's daughter,
I would not have become rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אִי לָא נָסֵיבְנָא כָּהֵנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second positive example, this time about wealth.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that marrying into כהונה brings wealth, for a תלמיד חכם
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא's personal testimony about his own wealth

steps.title: רב כהנא: Marrying a כהן's Daughter Got Me Exiled
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that if he had not married a כהנת, he would not have been exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: If I had not married a כהן's daughter, I would not have been exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: After several stories where marrying a כהנת brought blessing, רב כהנא tells his own story, where it brought trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a counter-example to steps 25 and 26, which showed marrying a כהנת brought success. רב כהנא was not a כהן, yet marrying into a כהן family led to his exile. The גמרא does not explain how this fits the תלמיד חכם / עם הארץ distinction of step 23, since רב כהנא was himself a great scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: a daughter of a כהן (a כהנת)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
If I had not married a daughter of a kohen,
I would not have been exiled.
phrases.notes: He had to flee from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אִי לָא נָסֵיבְנָא כָּהֵנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite personal experience to רב פפא's report that marrying a כהנת made him rich.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying a כהנת led to רב כהנא's exile.

steps.title: But You Were Exiled to a Place of Torah
steps.stepSummary: People object to רב כהנא that going to a place of Torah is not a real punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But you were exiled to a place of Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: People challenge רב כהנא's complaint. They say his "exile" was actually a good thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He went to ארץ ישראל, a center of Torah learning. Moving to such a place sounds like a blessing, not a punishment. So why does he count it as harm from marrying a כהנת?

phrases.english: They said to him:
But you were exiled to a place of Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְהָא לִמְקוֹם תּוֹרָה גְּלֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's claim that his exile was a bad result.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that marrying a כהנת harmed him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moving to a place of Torah is a benefit, so it should not count as a punishment.

steps.title: My Exile Was a Forced Escape
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that his exile was not a normal, free choice. He was forced to flee.
steps.simpleTranslation: I was not exiled the way people usually go into exile.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains that where he ended up is not the point. How he got there is what hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who move to a Torah center usually choose to go. רב כהנא had to run away from the authorities, so his leaving was a real hardship. That suffering is what he connects to marrying a כהנת.

phrases.english: I was not exiled the way people go into exile.
phrases.notes: He did not move by choice. He had to flee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the harm was the way he left, not the place he went.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His exile was just a move to a Torah center, which is a blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a forced escape, which is a real hardship.
steps.whatToRemember: Marrying a כהנת is not always a blessing. רב כהנא's forced flight is the counter-example to the stories of wealth.

steps.title: Enjoying Optional Feasts Leads to Exile
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that whoever enjoys a סעודת הרשות will end up exiled, and he proves it from verses in עמוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Anyone who enjoys an optional feast will end up exiled. It says: "And they eat lambs from the flock and calves out of the stall," and it is written: "Therefore now they will be exiled at the head of the exiles."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי שמעון's topic of meals that are not a מצוה (step 15), linked here by the theme of exile. Optional feasting leads to exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סעודת הרשות is a meal that is not a מצוה, such as a party just for enjoyment. The first verse describes people indulging in fancy meat, and a nearby verse says they will be exiled first. Putting the two together shows that luxurious feasting leads to exile.

keyTerms.meaning: an optional meal that is not a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a סעודת מצוה (like a wedding or ברית). It is only about meals eaten just for pleasure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who benefits from an optional feast
will end up exiled,
as it is stated: "And they eat lambs from the flock
and calves out of the midst of the stall,"
and it is written: "Therefore now they shall be exiled
at the head of the exiles."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדַת הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the word "exile" from רב כהנא's story and returns to רבי שמעון's rule about non-מצוה meals in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoying optional feasts leads to exile.

steps.title: The Harms of a Scholar Who Feasts Everywhere
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the many bad results for a תלמיד חכם who feasts excessively wherever he goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Any Torah scholar who feasts a lot everywhere will end up destroying his home, widowing his wife, and orphaning his children. He will forget his learning, many disputes will come upon him, and people will not listen to him. He disgraces the name of Heaven, his teacher, and his father, and he gives a bad name to himself, his children, and his grandchildren until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the theme of feasting. This time it focuses on a Torah scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves from his home (house, wife, children), to his Torah (forgetting, disputes, not being listened to), to his reputation (חילול השם and a bad family name). A scholar is a public model, so his indulgence damages far more than himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: A תלמיד חכם represents the Torah, so his behavior affects how people see Torah and his own family for generations.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַמַּרְבֶּה סְעוּדָּתוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Any Torah scholar who feasts excessively in every place,
will in the end destroy his house,
and widow his wife,
and orphan his chicks,
and his learning will be forgotten by him,
and many disputes will come upon him,
and his words will not be heeded,
and he desecrates the name of Heaven
and the name of his teacher and the name of his father,
and he causes a bad name for himself and his children

phrases.aramaic: וְלִבְנֵי בָנָיו עַד סוֹף כׇּל הַדּוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: and his grandchildren until the end of all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַמַּרְבֶּה סְעוּדָּתוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יצחק's warning about feasting and applies it to a Torah scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar who feasts everywhere brings ruin on his home, his learning, his reputation, and his descendants.

steps.title: What Is the Bad Name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the "bad name" mentioned in the ברייתא actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the last line of the ברייתא. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said his descendants would carry a bad name forever. The גמרא wants to know what that name actually sounds like.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of "שם רע" from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What bad name will the feasting scholar's children be called?

steps.title: Four Embarrassing Nicknames
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רבא, רב פפא, and רב שמעיה each give a nickname the scholar's son will be called.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They will call him "son of the oven-heater." רבא said: "son of the one who dances in taverns." רב פפא said: "son of the bowl-licker." רב שמעיה said: "son of the one who folds up and lies down."
steps.whatsHappening: Four אמוראים answer the question. Each gives an insulting nickname that will stick to the scholar's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each nickname mocks the father's feasting. One says he was always heating ovens to cook, one that he danced to entertain at parties, one that he licked the bowls clean, and one that he curled up drunk and fell asleep. The nickname begins with "son of," which shows how the shame passes down to his children.

keyTerms.meaning: folds up and lies down (sleeps it off, drunk)

steps.whatToRemember: Indulgent feasting by a תלמיד חכם leads to exile, ruin, and a lasting embarrassing reputation for his family, shown by these mocking nicknames.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They call him "son of the one who heats ovens."
Rava said:
"Son of the one who dances in taverns."
Rav Pappa said:
"Son of the one who licks bowls."
Rav Shemaya said:
"Son of the one who folds up and lies down."
phrases.notes: He folds his garment and crouches down, falling asleep drunk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: קָרוּ לֵיהּ בַּר מַחֵים תַּנּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bad name is a mocking nickname about the father's feasting. Four versions are given: oven-heater, tavern-dancer, bowl-licker, and drunk sleeper.

steps.title: Sell everything to marry a scholar's daughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man should give up all his possessions to marry the daughter of a תלמיד חכם. If he dies or is exiled, his sons will still become scholars. Marrying the daughter of an עם הארץ risks sons who are ignorant.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person should always sell everything he owns to marry the daughter of a Torah scholar. That way, if he dies or is exiled, he can be sure his sons will be Torah scholars. He should not marry the daughter of an ignoramus, because if he dies or is exiled, his sons will be ignoramuses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about choosing a wife. It is connected to the earlier topic of exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps talked about scholars who end up in exile. This ברייתא picks up that word, גולה, and asks what happens to the children when the father is gone. The answer is that the mother's home background will shape the sons, so a scholar's daughter will raise scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: Always — a general rule of good conduct
Ignoramus; a person unlearned in Torah
He is assured; he can be confident

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "if he dies or is exiled" does not mean the father's role doesn't matter. It means that even when the father cannot be there, the mother's background will still guide the children.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ
phrases.english: A person should always sell all that he has
and marry the daughter of a Torah scholar,
for if he dies or is exiled —
he is assured that his sons will be Torah scholars.
phrases.notes: Their mother, raised in a home of Torah, will see to their learning.

phrases.english: And he should not marry the daughter of an ignoramus,
for if he dies or is exiled —
his sons will be ignoramuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of scholars who feast and are exiled to a new ברייתא about marriage, linked by the theme of exile (גולה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man should sell all he owns to marry a scholar's daughter, since if he dies or is exiled, she will raise scholarly sons; marrying an עם הארץ's daughter risks ignorant sons.

steps.title: A good match is like grapes with grapes
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא repeats the advice to marry a scholar's daughter. It adds that one should also marry off one's own daughter to a תלמיד חכם. It compares a matching union to grapes joined with grapes, and a mismatched union to grapes joined with bramble berries.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person should always sell everything he owns to marry the daughter of a Torah scholar and to marry off his daughter to a Torah scholar. This is like grapes of a vine joined with grapes of a vine — something beautiful and accepted. He should not marry the daughter of an ignoramus. That is like grapes of a vine joined with berries of a bramble bush — something ugly...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same opening. This one adds two new points, and it continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא only spoke about the man's wife. This one adds the other direction: give your own daughter to a scholar too. It also gives a picture: two grapevines joined together fit naturally, while a grapevine joined to a thorny bramble is a bad and ugly mix.

keyTerms.meaning: And he should marry off his daughter
Berries of a bramble or thornbush

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a repeat of the first ברייתא. It is a separate ברייתא that adds marrying off one's daughter and the grapevine parable. Also, the sentence "דבר כעור" continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ
phrases.english: A person should always sell all that he has
and marry the daughter of a Torah scholar,
and marry off his daughter to a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: New point not found in the first ברייתא.

phrases.english: it is comparable to grapes of a vine with grapes of a vine,
something beautiful and acceptable.
And he should not marry the daughter of an ignoramus,
it is comparable to grapes of a vine with berries of a bramble,
something ugly
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם, מָשָׁל לְעִנְבֵי הַגֶּפֶן בְּעִנְבֵי הַגֶּפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that expands the first one by adding marrying off one's daughter to a scholar, and by giving the grapevine parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying into a scholar's family in both directions is like grapes joined with grapes, fitting and beautiful; marrying an עם הארץ's daughter is like grapes joined with bramble berries, unseemly.
